rationale: No race telemetry is supplied for this iteration, so this is a baseline draft built from the contract rather than from measured results. Speed: the run must cover about 4.5 m in under 3 s, so I set base_speed to 1.8 (near full drive, which gives PWM about 3685) to leave margin for the slower bends. Sensing: five sensors, 12 mm footprints, spaced 12 mm apart across x = -0.024 to +0.024 and placed 50 mm ahead of the axle. That spacing keeps the 25 mm tape covered by at least two sensors at all times and gives the sensors time to react before the wheels reach the bend. Weights run -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, so a tape offset to the left gives a positive signal, which steers left, as required. Control: kp = 4 gives a moderate steering response at a typical signal magnitude of 0.5 to 1. kd = 0.5 damps overshoot on the curves. ki = 0.1 is kept small to avoid integral windup on long bends. line_loss = last_direction, so the robot keeps turning the way it was last heading when the tape disappears, which suits sharp bends better than a fixed search. Geometry: a 0.12 m track and 0.03 m wheels give a responsive but stable base. Mass 0.8 kg and a 0.12 m body width keep the off-track allowance comfortable. Expected result: completion in about 2.6 to 3.0 s with a small rms error (under 0.02 m) and zero or one line-loss events. The main risks are oscillation at high speed and running wide on the slalom; the next iteration should use the telemetry to tune kp, kd and base_speed.
